bug_semantics: Unauthenticated HTTP/2 HEADERS with CR, LF, or NUL inside HPACK field values decode without error and are copied into Plug.Conn.req_headers. Bandit.HTTP2.Stream.read_headers/1 (and its pre-1.4.0 ancestors) checks pseudo-header placement/uniqueness, lowercase names, connection-specific headers, te, and content-length, but never inspects field values. HTTP/1 later rejects the same octets; HTTP/2 did not. Bandit itself is not a sink (logs use inspect/fixed strings; HTTP/2 responses are HPACK plus Plug put_resp_header), so impact is downstream log/header injection. A sibling gap in the same fix: duplicate :authority was accepted.
flaw_origin: The application-visible HTTP/2 path was first written in aa68cfc718ddcef62be5e5f5adff397e36c1bafb (2021-06-03): Bandit.HTTP2.Stream.run/5 built Plug.Conn with req_headers set to the raw HPACK-decoded header list and invoked the plug, with no CR/LF/NUL check. Immediate parent e9e78f5aa481fecd3eb6fc665a2c00582028912c still only IO.puts the headers. Later commits (9bc86b27 RFC7540§8.1 checks; #286/#307 stream refactor that created read_headers/1; HTTP/1-only #620) moved or partially hardened that path but never introduced the missing field-value rejection.

reasoning: CVE-2026-75484 is a published EEF CNA record (not withdrawn/rejected): HTTP/2 HPACK field values containing CR/LF/NUL reach conn.req_headers because read_headers/1 never validated values, while HTTP/1 does. Bandit is not itself a log/response-splitting sink; the transport-level acceptance is the bug. The CNA git range starts at fff06ef (1.4.0), which is the surviving reintroduction of the current HTTP2.Stream.read_headers/1 stack after #286 was reverted. That squash/reintroduce is not a BIC. Walking #286 members shows read_headers is a rename of recv_headers, which was a move of an incomplete RFC7540 checklist that itself post-dates the first Plug delivery. The smallest first-write of the flawed mechanism is aa68cfc718ddcef62be5e5f5adff397e36c1bafb: it first stuffed the HPACK-decoded header list into Plug.Conn.req_headers and called the plug. Immediate parent e9e78f5 still only printed the headers, so the application-visible path is absent there. 9bc86b27 later added pseudo-header/name/te checks and still omitted field values; that is incomplete hardening, not the introduction. The same omission is present in 1.3.0 stream_task.ex, so the CNA 1.4.0 floor is a current-stack/support window, not a clean origin. #620 (Claude co-authored) hardened only HTTP/1 and is irrelevant to BIC authorship. Fix d38cf046 lands the shared Bandit.Headers field-value check on HTTP/2 and is in 1.12.5, not 1.12.4.
